messages.author: 4074cf186f5bdce2
messages.subject: setting maxdist threshold in cleanGeno
parts:
Hi all,

I was wondering if anyone had thoughts setting the threshold for cleanGeno.

Say I'm working with a backcross and I know the species has high cross over interference could I set the threshold higher?

What about species where crossover interference is very low? Is the maxdist threshold valuable at all for those species?

Am I completely wrong to think that the level of cross over interference might be relevant to setting this threshold?

I appreciate your thoughts,

-Matthew

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] setting maxdist threshold in cleanGeno
parts:
Yes, if crossover interference is high, then maxdist could be set higher.
There's a trade-off between leaving in genotypes that are in error and omitting genotypes that are really correct.

Personally, I no longer try to clean up the genotypes. I want to identify and omit markers that are particularly badly behaved, but mostly I rely on error.prob in calc.genoprob() and est.map() to smooth over any genotyping errors.

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] setting maxdist threshold in cleanGeno
parts:
If you have low-density markers, it’s difficult to tell whether a particular genotype is an error. You can see that there are more double-crossovers then there should be, but you can’t tell which ones are errors.

If you have high-density markers, there will be more errors than you can carefully consider, individually.  

But really, the things is that we’re not trying to determine the genotypes but rather to map QTL or to estimate a genetic map, and for those tasks it’s perfectly fine to just leave the errors in and use methods that are tolerant to the presence of errors.

karl
